topic: Comparing Adding Subtracting Bar Graph Data Table Values
q: Two classes, Class A and Class B, each recorded the favorite fruit of the students in the class. The graph shows the results. Which fruit was the favorite of the most students in the two classes together?
key: Answer: B. Add the two bars for each fruit: apple 7 + 2 = 9, banana 4 + 6 = 10, grape 3 + 3 = 6, orange 5 + 4 = 9. Banana has the most, 10. A has the tallest single bar (7), but the question asks about both classes together.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Comparing Adding Subtracting Bar Graph Data Table Values · Wrong so far: 3/13 · New problem · Built on: Lower 3 QR #24 (her miss, middle third, 74% right)

topic: Finding MMMR given Bar Graph Data Table
q: The table shows four test scores for each of four students. What is the mode of this set of data?
key: Answer: B. The mode is the score that appears most often. 86 appears 3 times (Ana, Ben, Cara). 79, 88, and 95 appear only twice. D is the highest score, not the mode.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Finding MMMR given Bar Graph Data Table · Wrong so far: 2/11 · New problem · Built on: Lower 5 MA #17 (her miss, middle third, 83% right)

q: A box holds 48 crayons that are packed into groups of 6. If p represents the number of packs in the box, which equation can be used to find p?
key: Answer: D. p packs with 6 crayons in each make 48 crayons: 6 × p = 48 (so p = 8). B is backwards: try p = 8, and 48 × 8 is not 6. That is the PT6 MA #12 and QR10 #4 slip.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Matching Stories to Equations · Wrong so far: 2/8 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 MA #12 (her miss, middle third) and QR10 #4

q: The number machine performs the same operation on each input to create an output. What is the output for an input of 51?
key: Answer: C. Every output is 9 less than its input: 23 − 9 = 14, 42 − 9 = 33. So 51 − 9 = 42. D adds 9 instead of subtracting. B subtracts 10. A is the last output in the table, not the output for 51.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Input Output Tables · Wrong so far: 3/7 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 MA #13 (her miss, middle third; that rule was − 7, outputs smaller than inputs)

q: The table shows how a number machine changes each input number (△) into an output number (■). Which equation shows the rule for the number machine?
key: Answer: A. Check every row. 2 × 3 − 2 = 4, 4 × 3 − 2 = 10, 5 × 3 − 2 = 13, 7 × 3 − 2 = 19. B works only for 2, C only for 4, D only for 5.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Input Output Tables · Wrong so far: 3/7 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 QR #6 (first third) and QR10 #26 (her miss)

q: Which list shows 0.65, 58, and 23 in order from least to greatest?

choices.A: 0.65,  58,  23
choices.B: 23,  0.65,  58
choices.C: 58,  0.65,  23
choices.D: 58,  23,  0.65

key: Answer: C. Change each to a decimal: 5/8 = 0.625, 0.65, 2/3 ≈ 0.667. Least to greatest: 5/8, 0.65, 2/3. B is greatest to least. D puts the decimal last because it is written differently.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Comparing & Ordering Fractions & Decimals · Wrong so far: 10/24 · New problem · Built on: Lower 1 QR #22 and Lower 3 QR #20 (her misses, middle third); QR10 #13

q: Lena has 5 yards of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces that are each 8 inches long. There are 3 feet in 1 yard and 12 inches in 1 foot. How many 8-inch pieces can she cut?
key: Answer: C. 1 yard = 3 × 12 = 36 inches, so 5 yards = 180 inches. 180 ÷ 8 = 22 R4, so 22 full pieces (4 inches are left over). A uses 12 inches in a yard (her QR10 #11 slip). B is the number of feet. D rounds up, but a 4-inch piece is not a full piece.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: English Unit Conversions · Wrong so far: 2/3 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 QR #25 (her miss, middle third) and QR10 #11

q: A store sells a notebook for $4.50. The price of the notebook decreased by 12%. What is the price of the notebook now?
key: Answer: A. 12% of $4.50 is 0.12 × 4.50 = $0.54. The new price is 4.50 − 0.54 = $3.96. B subtracts 0.12 instead of 12% of the price (the "decreased by" slip). C adds 0.12. D increases by 12%.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Evaluating Percents of Numbers · Wrong so far: 1/1 · New problem · Built on: Official ISEE practice exercise (gid 1108, her MA3 #3 miss)

topic: Minimum Distance on Coordinate Plane / Grid
q: Use the grid to answer the question. How many units is the shortest distance from point A to point B if you can only move down or to the right?
key: Answer: C. Right: from x = −3 to x = 2 is 5 units (3 to reach 0, then 2 more). Down: from y = 4 to y = −2 is 6 units (4 to reach 0, then 2 more). 5 + 6 = 11. 9 and 10 come from missing a unit when crossing 0. Each grid square is half a unit, so counting squares gives 22; count by the axis numbers instead.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Minimum Distance on Coordinate Plane / Grid · Wrong so far: 1/1 · New problem · Built on: Official ISEE practice exercise (gid 1453, her MA3 #30 miss)

q:
□ + □ + △ = 23
□ + △ + △ = 19
What is the value of □?
key: Answer: C. Add the two lines: three □ and three △ make 23 + 19 = 42, so one □ and one △ make 42 ÷ 3 = 14. Take that away from the first line: □ + (□ + △) = 23, so □ = 23 − 14 = 9. Check the second line: 9 + 5 + 5 = 19. D stops at □ + △ = 14 (her QR9 #9 slip). B is △. A is □ − △.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Algebra with Geometric Shapes · Wrong so far: 3/7 · New problem · Built on: QR10 #27 type (parent pick); MA4 #5 shape; her QR9 #9 miss (stopped at the sum)

q:
Maya recorded information about the books in her class library. She listed the information in categories or groups.
1. Type of book: mystery, science, poetry
2. Language each book is written in
3. ?
Which information best completes Maya’s list?

choices.A: the number of pages in each book
choices.B: how many times each book was borrowed
choices.D: the color of each book’s cover

key: Answer: D. Type and language are categories (words, not numbers). Only the color of the cover is a category. A, B, and C are all numbers you count or measure. Find the one choice unlike the other three.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Data Collection & Random Sampling · Wrong so far: 2/4 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 QR #38 (her miss, last third, 18.4% right) and Lower 5 MA #30

q: How many numbers between 27 and 78 are multiples of 7?
key: Answer: D. The first multiple of 7 after 27 is 28 = 7 × 4. The last one before 78 is 77 = 7 × 11. Count 4 through 11: 11 − 4 + 1 = 8. C is her shortcut (78 − 27) ÷ 7 = 7 R2, which misses one.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Counting Multiples within a Range · Wrong so far: 3/10 · New problem · Built on: Lower 5 MA #29 (her miss, last third); QR9 #36, QR6 #28

topic: Identifying Correct Conclusions from Bar Graph Data Table
q: The stem-and-leaf plot shows the number of points a basketball team scored in each of 14 games, where 4 | 6 represents 46 points. Based on the data in the stem-and-leaf plot, which conclusion is true?

choices.A: The team scored at least 35 points in every game.
choices.B: The team scored 41 points in 3 games.
choices.C: The team scored 35 points in 3 games.
choices.D: The team scored 60 or more points in exactly 3 games.

key: Answer: B. Read each leaf with its stem. The 4 row has leaves 0, 1, 1, 1, 6, so 41 appears 3 times. A is false: the lowest score is 32. C is false: 35 appears only twice. D is false: only 60 and 64 are 60 or more, which is 2 games.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Identifying Correct Conclusions from Bar Graph Data Table · Wrong so far: 1/7 · New problem · Built on: Lower 2 QR #37 (her miss, last third, 41.7% right)

q: The price of a bike was increased by 20%. The amount of the increase was $16. What was the price of the bike before the increase?
key: Answer: B. The $16 increase is 20% of the price before the increase. 20% is one fifth, so the price was 16 × 5 = $80. C is the new price, 80 + 16. A takes the 16 away. D adds 16 to the new price again.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Percent Word Problems · Wrong so far: 12/34 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 MA #28 with increase wording (parent 11/11)

q: Maria did the problem 70 ÷ 9 × 124. Approximately what was her answer?
key: Answer: C. Work left to right: 70 ÷ 9 first. 72 ÷ 9 = 8, so 70 ÷ 9 is a little less than 8 (about 7.8). 7.8 × 124 is about 964: between 900 and 1,200. A comes from doing 9 × 124 first, as if the problem were 70 ÷ (9 × 124). B comes from rounding too much: 70 ÷ 10 × 120 = 840.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: Estimating Multiplication & Division · Wrong so far: 3/18 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 QR #36 (her miss, last third); parent 11/11: she adds parentheses that are not there

q: Three bottles hold 58 liter, 0.6 liter, and 710 liter of water. How much more water does the bottle with the most hold than the bottle with the least?
key: Answer: C. 5/8 = 0.625 and 7/10 = 0.7. In order: 0.6, 0.625, 0.7. Most minus least: 0.7 − 0.6 = 0.1. A is 0.625 − 0.6 and B is 0.7 − 0.625: each uses the middle bottle. D is 1 − 0.6.

q:
Mia reads the same number of pages each day to finish a book. The list shows what is known.
The number of pages in the book is □.
The number of pages she has already read is ☆.
The number of days she has left is ○.
Which equation will determine △, the number of pages she must read each day?
key: Answer: B. First find the pages still to read: □ − ☆. Share them over the days left: (□ − ☆) ÷ ○. Try numbers: a 200-page book, 50 pages read, 10 days left: 150 ÷ 10 = 15 pages a day. A gives 200 ÷ 10 − 50, which is less than 0. C adds the pages already read. D divides the wrong way.

topic: Nth Term, given Arithmetic Sequence, Progressive Pattern, etc.
q: In a sequence, each number is 7 more than the number before it. The 5th number in the sequence is 38. What is the 20th number in the sequence?
key: Answer: B. From the 5th number to the 20th number is 20 − 5 = 15 steps. 15 × 7 = 105, and 38 + 105 = 143. A takes 14 steps and C takes 16 steps (off by one). D takes 17.

q: Leo spent 2 56 hours at the library. Of that time, 1 14 hours were spent eating lunch and walking. How many minutes did Leo spend reading? (1 hour = 60 minutes)
key: Answer: A. 2 5/6 hours: 5/6 of 60 is 50, so it is 120 + 50 = 170 minutes. 1 1/4 hours: 1/4 of 60 is 15, so it is 60 + 15 = 75 minutes. 170 − 75 = 95. B is off by 10 (her QR9 #12 slip). C forgets the 1 whole hour in 1 1/4. D adds instead of subtracting.

q: Which expression is equivalent to 500 − 9 × (40 − 3)?
key: Answer: C. 9 × (40 − 3) = 9 × 40 − 9 × 3 = 360 − 27 = 333, and 500 − 333 = 167. Taking it away from 500 flips the second sign: 500 − 360 + 27 = 167. B keeps the minus (500 − 360 − 27 = 113). A multiplies only the 40. D subtracts before multiplying.

topic: Classification of Numbers, given a Set
q: Two numbers are greater than 1. One is an even number and the other is a prime number. What will always describe the product of the two numbers?
key: Answer: A. An even number times any whole number is even, so the product is always even. Try 4 × 3 = 12 and 2 × 5 = 10. B fails because of the even number. C fails: 12 is not prime. D fails: 2 × 3 = 6 is not a multiple of 4.

q: Jo has a roll with 3 yards of ribbon and a bag of 24 buttons. She wants to make 12 bookmarks. Each bookmark uses 10 inches of ribbon and 2 buttons. There are 3 feet in 1 yard and 12 inches in 1 foot. Which statement best explains whether Jo has enough ribbon?

choices.A: Since 3 × 12 = 36 is less than 120, Jo does not have enough ribbon.
choices.B: Since 3 × 36 = 108 is less than 120, Jo does have enough ribbon.
choices.C: Since 24 buttons is enough for 12 × 2 = 24 buttons, Jo does have enough ribbon.
choices.D: Since 3 × 36 = 108 is less than 120, Jo does not have enough ribbon.

key: Answer: D. 1 yard = 3 × 12 = 36 inches, so 3 yards = 108 inches. 12 bookmarks need 12 × 10 = 120 inches. 108 is less than 120, so she does not have enough. A uses 12 inches in a yard (her QR10 #11 slip): the conclusion happens to be right, but the reason is wrong. B has the right numbers and the wrong conclusion. C is about buttons, which the question does not ask.
ref: Tier: Hard · Topic: English Unit Conversions · Wrong so far: 2/3 · New problem · Built on: Lower 6 QR #25 (her miss, middle third) and QR10 #11 (her miss), same format as QR10 #11

q: Omar builds picture frames. The first rectangular frame he builds has a perimeter of 30 centimeters (cm). The length of one of the sides is shown. If the unknown side length of the next frame he builds is tripled, by what amount will the unknown side length increase?
key: Answer: B. The two 9 cm sides use 18 cm, so the two unknown sides share 30 − 18 = 12 cm, and each is 6 cm. Tripled, it becomes 18 cm. The increase is 18 − 6 = 12 cm. A is the unknown side itself. C is the new length, not the increase. D is 30 − 9.

topic: Finding Area/Perimeter of Rectangle, given Length & Width
q: The perimeter of a square is 36 centimeters. A rectangle with a width of 3 centimeters has the same area as the square. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in centimeters?
key: Answer: D. Square side: 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so its area is 81. Rectangle length: 81 ÷ 3 = 27. Perimeter: 27 + 3 + 27 + 3 = 60. A stops at the length. B assumes the same perimeter. C adds only the two lengths.

q: The base of a triangle is 12 centimeters (cm). Which statement correctly compares the value of A to the height of the triangle? (A = 12 × base × height)

choices.A: The value of A is always 12 the value of the height.
choices.B: The value of A is always 12 times the value of the height.
choices.C: The value of A can be the same as the value of the height.
choices.D: The value of A is always 6 times the value of the height.

key: Answer: D. Put the base into the formula: A = 1/2 × 12 × height = 6 × height. Check: height 2 gives A = 12, which is 6 times 2. A uses only the 1/2. B uses only the 12.

topic: 3D shape from its net (unfolding a solid)
q: The net shown is folded to make a cube. Which symbol will be on the face opposite the face with the ★?
key: Answer: D. When the net folds, the ★ square folds over the top of the row of four squares and the ◆ square folds under it, so they end up on opposite faces. ▲, ●, and ♥ are all on the row of four, which goes around the sides, so each of them touches the ★ face. A is right under the ★ on the net, but it folds to be next to it, not across from it.
